summary: Added a non-colliding clipos-dev Compose stack with host ports 5433/6380/9002/9003, a Pydantic infrastructure health contract and Compose JSON parser, six parser regression tests, an idempotent read-only infrastructure_health.sh gate, Make targets, CI startup/poll/cleanup coverage, and developer documentation. All executable quality gates passed in this environment; the live container lifecycle gate was blocked by Docker socket permissions and the shared Git worktree index remains read-only, so the changes are staged in the working tree but not committed.
contracts_changed: docker compose ps JSON -> InfrastructureHealth parser contract

tests.name: Infrastructure parser unit tests
tests.evidence: 6 passed in 0.12s using CLIP-001's Python 3.14 virtualenv (pytest 9.1.1, pydantic 2.13.5) because this worktree has no local .venv and network/package installation is unavailable.

tests.name: Existing API unit tests except /health
tests.evidence: 7 passed (2 audit + 1 modules + 4 registry), no failures.

tests.name: Existing API /health TestClient test
tests.evidence: The inherited CLIP-001 virtualenv TestClient/httpx/anyio stack hangs on Python 3.14 when invoking the unchanged GET /health endpoint; faulthandler showed the request blocked in anyio run_sync. This test is unchanged and was green on the CLIP-001 CI environment (GitHub Actions run 37383281375). It should be rerun in the orchestrator Python 3.12 environment.

tests.name: API lint
tests.evidence: All checks passed! using CLIP-001's available ruff 0.16.10; 3 initial import-order/annotation findings were auto-fixed and rechecked.

tests.name: Operator port collision grep gate
tests.evidence: No host-side 5432 or 6379 mapping remains; mappings are 5433:5432, 6380:6379, 9002:9000, and 9003:9001.

tests.name: Live infrastructure stack health
tests.command: docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --wait && bash scripts/infrastructure_health.sh
tests.evidence: Docker CLI responds for config parsing but container API access is denied: "permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock". No containers were started; orchestrator must execute the two-cycle up/health/down acceptance.

tests.name: Health script syntax and stdlib fallback
tests.evidence: Exit 0. The script is read-only, timeout behavior is delegated to Docker, and it exits 1 on degraded/empty output with the same JSON contract.

tests.name: CI workflow YAML parse
tests.evidence: Parsed successfully; test job now starts the stack, polls infrastructure_health.sh up to 90 seconds, and always cleans up with down -v. Report still combines validate and test.

tests.name: Web typecheck
tests.evidence: Node/npm/npx are unavailable in this sandbox; apps/web was untouched.

security_rights_budget_impact: No secrets, external side effects, rights actions, publishing paths, tenant data, privileged operations, or spend are introduced. Existing dev-only credentials remain explicitly local-only. The health command is read-only and CI cleanup runs on always().
known_limitations: The Docker socket rejects container operations for this sandbox user, so live two-cycle stack health evidence must be produced by the orchestrator.
Git commit is unavailable because /srv/clipos/clipOS/.git/worktrees/CLIP-002/index.lock is on a read-only filesystem; changes remain visible as working-tree modifications on agent/CLIP-002.
GET /health TestClient execution is an inherited Python 3.14/httpx compatibility issue in the borrowed virtualenv, not a code change; CI Python 3.12 remains the authoritative environment.
blockers: Docker container API access is denied (permission denied on unix:///var/run/docker.sock).
Git commit is blocked by a read-only shared .git worktree index.
